title: Electric and Magnetic Field Devices for Stimulation of Biological Tissues
protocol: Select an axisymmetric 2D configuration.
Choose Electric Current interface to compute EFs.
Create geometries using Rectangle tool with dimensions specified in Units section.
Build all objects in Geometry.
Create selections for metal domain.
Right-click Explicit and rename it to Metal.
Click Boundaries and choose Terminal on the Physics Toolbar.
Locate the Boundary Selection section in the Terminal Settings window and choose Terminal boundaries from the Selection list.
Choose Voltage from the Terminal list and type 100 V.
Click Add Material on the Home Toolbar to open the Add Material window.
Search for air and stainless-steel and add them to the Model Builder window.
Click Blank Material on the Home Toolbar and add three new blank materials for culture media, scaffold (hydrogel), and polystyrene (culture well-plate).
Select a blank material to assign dielectric properties.
Locate the Material Properties list in the Material settings window and select relative permittivity and electric conductivity from the Basic Properties option list.
Assign each material to the geometries previously built.
Select the air material from the Model Builder window, then select the domains that correspond to air from the Graphic window.
Repeat this step for all materials created.
Make sure that each domain corresponds to the correct material.
Build mesh.
Right-click Mesh 1 in the Model Builder window and select Free Triangular.
Select Size.
In the Mesh Settings window, select Mesh Controlled by the User from the Sequence Type list.
Expand the Mesh options in the Model Builder window and click Size.
Locate Element Size Parameters in the Size Setting window.
Type 1 mm for maximum element size.
Type 0.002 mm for minimum element size.
Type 1.1 for maximum edge growth rate.
Type 0.2 for curvature factor.
Type 1 for resolution of narrow regions.
Expand the Mesh options in the Model Builder window and click Free Triangular 1.
Select all domains to be meshed.
Click Build All in the Mesh Setting window.
Create study.
Click Study 1 in the Model Builder window.
Locate the Study Settings section and clear the Generate default plots check box.
Expand the Study 1 node and click Step 1: Frequency Domain.
Type 60 kHz in the Frequencies text field in the Frequency Domain Settings window.
Calculate study.
Click Show Default Solver on the Study toolbar.
Expand the Study 1 Solver Configurations node in the Model Builder window.
Expand the Solution 1 (sol1) node in the Model Builder window.
Click Stationary Solver 1 in the Stationary Solver Settings window.
Type 1e-6 in the Relative Tolerance text field in the General section.
Click Compute on the Study Toolbar.
Plot results.
Select Results section on the Home toolbar.
Add 2D Plot Group.
Right-click 2D Plot Group 1 and choose Surface.
Locate the Data section in the Surface Settings window and select Precursor.
In the Expression section, click the plus (+) symbol to open a new window.
From the selection list, locate Model - Component 1 - Electric Currents - Electric.
Select ec.normE - EF Norm.
Click Graphic in the Surface Settings window to plot the results.
Create geometries.
Select Geometry in the Model Builder.
Choose mm in the Units section.
Select Rectangle on the Geometry Toolbar.
Type dimensions of each component in the Size and Shape box of the Rectangle Window Settings.
Click Build All Objects.
Add materials by clicking Add Material on the Home Toolbar.
Search for air and copper, then add them to the Model Builder window.
Open Magnetic Fields Settings window from the Model Builder.
Choose Frequency Domain equation from the Equation Form list under Equation list.
Choose From solver in the Frequency list.
Locate Ampere's Law in the Magnetic Field list in the Model Builder window.
Type 293.15[K] in Temperature, and 1[atm] in Absolute Pressure from the Inputs Model list.
Select Solid from the Material type list in the Ampere's Law Settings window.
Ensure Electric conductivity, Relative permittivity, and Relative Permeability correspond to From material in the list.
Locate Axial Symmetry on the Magnetic Field list in the Model Builder window.
Highlight the axial symmetry line in both Boundary Selection list and Graphic window.
Locate Magnetic Isolation on the Magnetic Field list in the Model Builder window.
Highlight boundaries from the geometry in both Boundary Selection list and Graphic window.
Locate Initial Values on the Magnetic Field list in the Model Builder window.
Select geometries previously built and include them in the Domain Selection from the Initial Values Settings window.
Introduce coil features.
Locate Multiple Coil on the Magnetic Field list in the Model Builder window.
Select the geometry that represents the coil and include it in the Domain Selection from the Multiple Coil Settings window.
Locate the Multiple Coil list on the Multiple Coil Setting window.
Select Current for the Coil excitation.
Type 1[A] in the Coil current list, 450 in the Number of turns, and 6e7[S/m] in the Coil conductivity.
Choose North American cable diameter (Brown & Sharpe) from the list for the Coil wire cross-sectional area.
Type 18 in the AWG option.
Ensure Relative permittivity and Relative Permeability correspond to From material in the list.
Build mesh.
Select Mesh Controlled by the physics from the Sequence Type list.
Select Extremely fine under Element Size Parameters.
Mesh all domains and click Build All.
Create study.
Click Study 1 in the Model Builder window.
Clear the Generate default plots check box in the Study Settings section.
Expand Step 2: Frequency Domain within Study 1 node.
Type 60 Hz in the Frequencies text field of the Frequency Domain Settings window.
Calculate study.
Click Show Default Solver on the Study toolbar.
Expand the Study 1 Solver Configurations node in the Model Builder window.
Expand the Solution 1 (sol1) node in the Model Builder window.
Click Stationary Solver 1 in the Stationary Solver Settings window.
Type 1e-6 in the Relative tolerance text field under General section.
Click Compute on the Study Toolbar.
Plot results.
Select Results section on the Home toolbar and add 2D Plot Group.
Right-click 2D Plot Group 1 in the Model Builder window and choose Surface.
Locate the Data section in the Surface Settings window and select Precursor.
Locate the Expression section in the Surface Settings window.
Click in the plus (+) symbol to open a new window.
Select mf.normB - Magnetic flux density Norm from the selection list (Model - Component 1 - Magnetic Field - Magnetic).
Click on Graphic in the Surface Settings window to plot the results.
Prepare the PCB using a third-party manufacturing service.
Place all components on the PCB with antistatic tweezers.
Solder all components using tin solder and a soldering iron.
Manufacture a plastic case with input connectors for protection.
Implement three input connectors to energize the circuit (12 V, -12 V and ground).
Use two input connectors to connect the electrodes.
Include three switches to change resistor combinations to obtain four output voltages.
Assemble the electronic circuit into the plastic case.
Manufacture two parallel stainless-steel electrodes (200 x 400 x 2 mm).
Solder input connectors to each edge of the electrodes.
Locate electrodes over Teflon or acrylic supports to eliminate contact with metal surfaces.
Sterilize the electrodes using an autoclave at 394.15 K for 30 minutes.
Sterilize wires in contact with the incubator using ultraviolet overnight.
Test the electrical stimulation device.
Adjust the power supply to generate an output voltage of +12 V and -12 V between the ground and positive/negative terminals.
Verify the output voltage with a multimeter.
Connect each output of the power supply in the correct input of the electrical stimulator (+12 V, -12 V and ground).
Connect each electrode in the correct input connector of the electrical stimulator.
Place a culture well-plate between the electrodes.
Verify the output signal with an oscilloscope.
Adjust the switches of the electrical stimulator to generate four output voltages (50, 100, 150, and 200 Vp-p).
Ensure cables are not tangled when transferring or removing electrodes from the incubator.
Disconnect cables from the oscillator before removing electrodes from the incubator.
Never place electrodes without acrylic or Teflon supports.
Choose a length (h) of 250 mm for the coil.
Select a current of 1 A for the coil operation.
Set Bint to 2 mT.
Wind AWG 18 copper wire around a PVC tube with dimensions 250 mm in length and 84 mm in diameter, completing 450 turns.
Build a PMMA support to ensure well-plates are centered within the coil for uniform MF exposure.
Construct a transformer with an output of 1 A - 6 V AC to achieve a maximum MF of 2 mT using an input voltage of 110 V AC at 60 Hz.
Connect the transformer directly to the outlet.
Insert a variable resistor (rheostat) in the circuit to adjust current and generate MFs from 1 to 2 mT.
Install a fuse into the circuit for protection.
Sterilize wires contacting the incubator with ultraviolet light overnight.
Wrap the coil with transparent stretch film and sterilize it using ethanol.
Use a teslameter to measure MF magnitude inside the coil, placing the probe at the center of the coil.
Vary the MF magnitude.
Use a rheostat to modify the resistance of the circuit.
Set a resistance value of 0.7 Ω to generate MFs of 1 mT.
Ensure cables are not tangled when transferring or removing the solenoid from the incubator.
Disconnect cables from the transformer before removing the solenoid from the incubator.
Never place the solenoid without the PMMA support.
Firmly grasp both PMMA support from the base and the solenoid when transferring or removing from the incubator.
